newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares hover around five-month lows.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares hover around five-month lows.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange hovered around five-month lows in quiet trade on Saturday as falls in ex-dividend shares offset blue-chip gains.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index closed at 150.31 points, just 0.16 percent above Wednesday's close of 150.22, its lowest level since late November.

Brokers said institutional demand pushed up Jordan Cement Factory, which rose 0.06 dinars to 3.78 dinars, and Jordan National Bank, which clawed back some of its recent losses to close at 1.75 dinars, also up 0.06 dinars.
Trade in the bank and cement factory accounted for one third of Saturday's 322,000 dinars ($455,000).
Arab Bank also rose two dinars to 255 dinars in turnover of 36,000 dinars.

But those blue-chip gains were matched by falls in Housing Bank, which approved a 0.2 dinar dividend at its general meeting on Friday, and a handful of other shares which went ex-dividend at the end of last week.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 20 to 10, with another four trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.53 percent to 79.55 points, 4.61 percent down from the start of the year.
